title: Private: structured verification + install provenance events (logs + metrics hooks)
author: Kevin Osei
release_notes:
- Private deployments now emit structured JSON events for offline bundle verification + install provenance (success/failure) with stable schema v1.
- Adds metrics hooks (counters + latency histograms) for verification outcomes and override usage.
description:
Context: As part of offline signed bundles for Redwood Private, we need an auditable, machine-parseable trail of (a) bundle verification outcomes and (b) what was installed (provenance). Today we have a mix of human-readable installer logs and a few ad-hoc strings in the control-plane bootstrapper; this makes support + compliance exports painful and makes it hard to build durable dashboards/alerts.

This PR adds a stable, versioned structured event schema and emits events from the Private installation/verification flow. Events are JSON lines written to the existing Private audit log location (same lifecycle/permissions), and are also exposed as metrics hooks for environments that scrape Prometheus. No outbound calls; all data remains local to the customer environment.

What’s included: (1) New event schema (schema_version=1) with explicit event types: private.bundle.verify.started, private.bundle.verify.succeeded, private.bundle.verify.failed, private.install.provenance.recorded, private.bundle.verify.override_used. (2) Consistent correlation fields: request_id (generated per run), install_id (stable for the install attempt), bundle_id (from bundle manifest), bundle_manifest_sha256, release_version, and build metadata (commit_sha, build_id) when available. (3) Security/privacy guardrails: no raw artifact paths, no container registry credentials, no key material; signature metadata is limited to key_fingerprint + signature_alg and only when present. Failure payloads include error_code + sanitized error_message (no stack traces by default) and a deterministic failure_stage value. (4) Metrics hooks: counters for verify_success/verify_failure/override_used and a histogram for verification_latency_ms. Metrics are tagged with outcome + stage + schema_version; bundle_id is intentionally NOT used as a label to avoid unbounded cardinality.

Implementation notes: Events are emitted via a small library (pkg/private/events) used by the offline verification command and by the install pipeline component that writes provenance after unpack/install. The writer supports stdout/stderr mode for tests and a file-backed JSONL sink in production. The sink does atomic append with file locking on Linux to avoid interleaving when multiple components write.

Testing: Adds unit tests for schema serialization and redaction, and integration tests that run the verification path and assert JSONL output includes required fields and stable error_code mapping. Also adds a small golden test fixture for one success + one failure event.

Follow-ups (out of scope): wiring these events into the redwood-private-installer repo CLI output formatting (tracked in ENG-3914) and exporting to customer SIEM via optional forwarder (future).
commits: pkg/private/events: introduce Event interface + JSONL sink (schema v1)
private/offline_verify: emit verify started/success/failure + latency measurement
private/install: record install provenance event after successful install stage
metrics: add verification counters + latency histogram hooks (no high-card labels)
tests: schema validation, redaction tests, golden fixtures, integration coverage
docs: internal comments + event field reference in code
review_conversation:
Allison Grant (Observability): Please confirm we’re not using bundle_id as a metric label; that’ll explode cardinality in real deployments. Also can we standardize field names to match our existing JSON log conventions (snake_case vs camelCase)?

Kevin Osei (Author): Good catch. Bundle ID is included in JSONL events but metrics only tag outcome/stage/schema_version. I also switched all event fields to snake_case to match our audit logs, and added a schema_version int to every event.

Marcus Lin (Security): Two asks: (1) don’t log full signer key IDs that could be tied to internal KMS resources; keep to a fingerprint. (2) Ensure error_message is sanitized (no stack traces, no file paths) unless debug mode is explicitly enabled.

Kevin Osei (Author): Updated. We now log key_fingerprint (SHA-256 of public key bytes) and signature_alg only. Error messages go through a sanitizer that strips filesystem paths + known secret patterns; stack traces only appear if REDWOOD_PRIVATE_DEBUG_LOGS=1 (off by default). Added tests for path redaction.

Ethan Park (Installer/Control Plane): I’d like to see deterministic error_code mapping. Right now verify.go returns raw errors which makes support automation hard.

Kevin Osei (Author): Added errors.go with a typed VerifyErrorCode enum (MANIFEST_MISSING, CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, SIGNATURE_INVALID, SIGNATURE_MISSING, SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED, IO_ERROR). Events now emit error_code + failure_stage. Updated integration tests to assert the mapping.

Priya Natarajan (Platform): Can we ensure file writes are safe with concurrent writers? In some deployments verification and install steps may overlap during retries.

Kevin Osei (Author): Implemented file locking via flock on Linux and a buffered writer. Also added a test that concurrently emits events and asserts well-formed JSON lines (no interleaving).

Approvals: Allison Grant approved after metrics label fix; Marcus Lin approved after key fingerprint + sanitization change; Ethan Park approved after error_code mapping; Priya Natarajan approved after file locking update.
ci_notes: Initial CI run failed in integration-tests (offline/hermetic) due to a golden fixture mismatch (field ordering + timestamp formatting). Fixed by making timestamp RFC3339Nano and sorting JSON keys during golden generation. Re-run succeeded.
merge_outcome: Merged into main; will ship with the next Redwood Private offline bundle verification milestone.
